transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

To be honest, I'm here because I just can't shake this fear of putting on weight, so I keep cutting back on what I eat. My family keeps insisting that I'm already too thin, which is why I reluctantly agreed to come in today.

Do you feel overweight or think certain parts of your body are too fat even though other people say you are very thin? Or do you know you’re underweight but still restrict food mainly because you’re afraid of gaining weight?

I wouldn't say I feel fat, but I get this rush of panic that I'll balloon up overnight if I eat a normal meal. My wife and doctors keep telling me I'm too thin, but I honestly think they're overreacting to a few skipped meals. To me, keeping my weight down just shows that I'm finally taking my health and discipline seriously.
Have you noticed your weight dropping to clearly below what’s healthy for your height, and if so, do you still feel it’s not a serious problem or that staying this thin is important to you?

My weight has definitely dropped—my pants hang off me now and my wedding ring is loose, but I actually feel a sense of pride when guys at basketball say I look "shredded." I don't think it's a serious problem and feel others are overreacting, because to me, it's just about being disciplined and taking my health seriously despite feeling cold or lightheaded sometimes.

What is your current height and weight, and about how much weight have you lost over what period of time? Have you had any fainting, heart palpitations, or times when a doctor said your heart rate or blood pressure was dangerously low?

I'm not actually sure about my exact weight or the precise amount of weight I've lost overall. However, I have passed out and gotten really lightheaded while working at the auto shop recently, which has made it hard to finish my work.
Have you ever had episodes where you ate a large amount of food and felt out of control, or done things like vomiting, using laxatives/diuretics, or exercising excessively to prevent weight gain?

No, I've never lost control and binged on food, and I've never thrown up or used laxatives to keep my weight down. It's actually the exact opposite for me; I strictly limit my portions, skip meals, and cut back even further because of how terrified I am of gaining weight.
When you look in the mirror or think about your body, do you believe you are still too heavy or that certain body parts are too fat, even though others say you are very thin?

I don't look in the mirror and think I'm fat; I actually see myself as lean and finally in good shape. It's more about this constant, intense fear of *becoming* heavy, which is why I'm always checking the scale to make sure the number doesn't go up even a little bit.

Is your body weight or shape one of the main things that determines how you feel about yourself or your self-worth? Or is the restriction mostly about preventing future weight gain even though you already see yourself as thin?

Yes, my weight and shape are definitely tied to my self-worth, and looking lean and "shredded" gives me a strong sense of pride and discipline. I don't see myself as too thin like everyone else does; keeping my weight down is how I maintain control and avoid the intense panic of ballooning up if I eat more.

He denies binge eating and purging, supporting anorexia nervosa, restrictive type.
